knowledge_point.title: Evaluating Surface Integrals Over Parametric Surfaces

question.:question/problem:
Evaluate the surface integral 

$$
{∬}_{S}(2x+y+z)\,\text{d}S,
$$

where the parametric surface $S$ is defined by 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨2u-v,\,3u+2,\,u+2v⟩
$$

 
over the domain $D=\{(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le 1,\,-1\le v\le 1\}.$

*Hint: You can use the fact that $‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖=\sqrt{70}.$*
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the surface integral of a scalar function $f$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A.
$$

Notice that we are told that the norm of the fundamental vector product is

$$
‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖=\sqrt{70}.
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $f(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(u,v)) & =(2x+y+z)\,{|}_{x=2u-v\,y=3u+2\,z=u+2v} \\  & =2(2u-v)+(3u+2)+(u+2v) \\  & =8u+2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our surface integral can be written as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,(8u+2)\sqrt{70}\,\text{d}A \\  & =\sqrt{70}{∬}_{D}\,(8u+2)\,\text{d}A \\  & =\sqrt{70}{\int }_{0}^{1}(8u+2)\,\text{d}u\cdot {\int }_{-1}^{1}\,\text{d}v \\  & =\sqrt{70}\cdot [4{u}^{2}+2u]_{0}^{1}\cdot [u]_{-1}^{1} \\  & =\sqrt{70}\cdot 6\cdot 2 \\  & =12\sqrt{70}.\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluate the surface integral 

$$
{∬}_{S}4xy\,\text{d}S,
$$

where the parametric surface $S$ is defined by the equations

$$
x=u,\,y=v,\,z=6-3u-2v
$$

for $0\le u\le 2$ and $0\le v\le \frac{5}{2}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the surface integral of a scalar function $f$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A.
$$

In vector form, our surface has the equation 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u,\,v,\,6-3u-2v⟩.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(6-3u-2v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,-3⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(6-3u-2v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,-2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & -3 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & -3 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨3,\,2,\,1⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

and 

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖ & =‖⟨3,\,2,\,1⟩‖ \\  & =\sqrt{{3}^{2}+{2}^{2}+{1}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{9+4+1} \\  & =\sqrt{14}.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $f(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(u,v)) & =4xy\,{|}_{x=u\,y=v\,z=6-3u-2v} \\  & =4uv\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, if we denote 

$$
D=\{(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le 2,\,0\le v\le \frac{5}{2}\},
$$

our surface integral can be written as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}4xy\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,4uv\sqrt{14}\,\text{d}A \\  & =\sqrt{14}{∬}_{D}\,4uv\,\text{d}A \\  & =\sqrt{14}{\int }_{0}^{2}2u\,\text{d}u\cdot {\int }_{0}^{\frac{5}{2}}2v\,\text{d}v \\  & =\sqrt{14}\cdot [{u}^{2}]_{0}^{2}\cdot [{v}^{2}]_{0}^{\frac{5}{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{14}[(4)-(0)]\cdot [(\frac{25}{4})-(0)] \\  & =\sqrt{14}\cdot 4\cdot \frac{25}{4} \\  & =25\sqrt{14}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the surface integral of a scalar function $f$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\,\text{d}A.
$$

Previously, we determined that our surface can be parametrized as

$$
r(x,\theta )=⟨x,\,2{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,2{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ⟩,\,x\in [0,1],\,\theta \in [0,2\pi ),
$$

and the norm of the fundamental vector product is

$$
‖{r}_{x}^{′}\times {r}_{\theta }^{′}‖=2{x}^{2}\sqrt{16{x}^{2}+1}.
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(x,\theta )$ into $d(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}d(r(x,\theta )) & =\frac{x({y}^{2}+{z}^{2})}{\sqrt{16{x}^{2}+1}} \\  & =\frac{x((2{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )^{2}+(2{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )^{2})}{\sqrt{16{x}^{2}+1}} \\  & =\frac{4{x}^{5}({cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta )}{\sqrt{16{x}^{2}+1}} \\  & =\frac{4{x}^{5}}{\sqrt{16{x}^{2}+1}}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our surface integral can be written as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}d(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}d(r(x,\theta ))‖{r}_{x}^{′}\times {r}_{\theta }^{′}‖\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,\frac{4{x}^{5}}{\sqrt{16{x}^{2}+1}}\cdot 2{x}^{2}\sqrt{16{x}^{2}+1}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,8{x}^{7}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}8{x}^{7}\,\text{d}x\cdot {\int }_{0}^{2\pi }\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =[{x}^{8}]_{0}^{1}\cdot [\theta ]_{0}^{2\pi } \\  & =(1-0)\cdot (2\pi -0) \\  & =2\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the surface integral of a scalar function $f$ over $S$ is given by

$$

$$

In vector form, our surface has the equation 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u+v,\,u,\,v⟩.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,1,\,0⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖ & =‖⟨1,\,-1,\,-1⟩‖ \\  & =\sqrt{{1}^{2}+-{1}^{2}+-{1}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{1+1+1} \\  & =\sqrt{3}.\end{aligned}

$$

$$

$$

where the parametric surface $S$ is defined by the equations

$$

$$

for $0\le u\le 1$ and $0\le v\le 2.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the surface integral of a scalar function $f$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A.
$$

In vector form, our surface has the equation 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u+v,\,u-v,\,0⟩.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u-v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(0)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,1,\,0⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u-v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(0)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,-1,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,0,\,-2⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

and 

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖ & =‖⟨0,\,0,\,-2⟩‖ \\  & =\sqrt{{0}^{2}+{0}^{2}+(-2)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{0+0+4} \\  & =\sqrt{4} \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $f(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(u,v)) & =xy+z\,{|}_{x=u+v\,y=u-v\,z=0} \\  & =(u+v)(u-v) \\  & ={u}^{2}-{v}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, if we denote 

$$
D={(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le 1,\,0\le v\le 2},
$$

our surface integral can be written as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}(xy+z)\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,({u}^{2}-{v}^{2})\cdot 2\,\text{d}A \\  & =2{∬}_{D}\,({u}^{2}-{v}^{2})\,\text{d}A \\  & =2{\int }_{0}^{2}({\int }_{0}^{1}({u}^{2}-{v}^{2})\,\text{d}u)\text{d}v \\  & =2{\int }_{0}^{2}{[\frac{{u}^{3}}{3}-{v}^{2}u]}_{0}^{1}\,\text{d}v \\  & =2{\int }_{0}^{2}(\frac{1}{3}-{v}^{2})\text{d}v \\  & =2{[\frac{v}{3}-\frac{{v}^{3}}{3}]}_{0}^{2} \\  & =2[\frac{2}{3}-\frac{8}{3}] \\  & =-4.\end{aligned}
$$

where the parametric surface $S$ is defined by the equations

for $0\le u\le 1$ and $0\le v\le 3.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the surface integral of a scalar function $f$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A.
$$

In vector form, our surface has the equation 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨2u,\,-3v,\,4v⟩.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(2u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(-3v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(4v)⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\,0,\,0⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(2u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(-3v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(4v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,-3,\,4⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -3 & 4\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ -3 & 4\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & -3\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,-8,\,-6⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖ & =‖⟨0,\,-8,\,-6⟩‖ \\  & =\sqrt{{0}^{2}+(-8)^{2}+(-6)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{0+64+36} \\  & =\sqrt{100} \\  & =10.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the surface integral of a scalar function $f$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A.

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(u,v)) & =(3x-2y+3z)\,{|}_{x=2u+v\,y=2u+v\,z=-v} \\  & =3(2u+v)-2(2u+v)+3(-v) \\  & =2(u-v)\end{aligned}

$$

$$

Previously, we determined that our surface can be parametrized as

$$
r(x,\theta )=⟨x,\,2{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,2{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ⟩,\,x\in [0,\frac{1}{2}],\,\theta \in [0,2\pi ),
$$

and the norm of the fundamental vector product is

$$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}d(r(x,\theta )) & =\frac{x({y}^{2}+{z}^{2})}{\sqrt{16{x}^{2}+1}} \\  & =\frac{x((2{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )^{2}+(2{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )^{2})}{\sqrt{16{x}^{2}+1}} \\  & =\frac{4{x}^{5}({cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta )}{\sqrt{16{x}^{2}+1}} \\  & =\frac{4{x}^{5}}{\sqrt{16{x}^{2}+1}}\end{aligned}

$$\iint_S(x-y)\,\text{d}S,$$

where $r(u,v)=⟨2u+3v,\,2u-3v,\,2v⟩$ for $0\le u\le 2$ and $0\le v\le 3.$

*Hint: $‖r_u′\times r_v′‖=4\sqrt{11}.$*

{{field-1}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the surface integral of a scalar function $f$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A.
$$

Notice that we are told that the norm of the fundamental vector product is

$$
‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖=4\sqrt{11}.
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $f(x,y,z):$

$$f(r(u,v))=(2u+3v)-(2u-3v)=6v.$$

Therefore, our surface integral can be written as

$$\begin{aligned}\iint_S(x-y)\,\text{d}S&=\iint_D f(r(u,v))‖r_u′\times r_v′‖\,\text{d}A\\&=4\sqrt{11}\iint_D 6v\,\text{d}A\\&=4\sqrt{11}\int_0^{3}6v\,\text{d}v\cdot\int_0^{2}1\,\text{d}u\\&=4\sqrt{11}[3v^{2}]_0^{3}[u]_0^{2}\\&=4\sqrt{11}(27-0)(2-0)\\&=216\sqrt{11}.\end{aligned}$$

$$\iint_S(x-y)\,\text{d}S,$$

where $r(u,v)=⟨u+2v,\,u-2v,\,3v⟩$ for $0\le u\le 3$ and $0\le v\le 1.$

*Hint: $‖r_u′\times r_v′‖=\sqrt{34}.$*

{{field-1}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the surface integral of a scalar function $f$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A.
$$

Notice that we are told that the norm of the fundamental vector product is

$$
‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖=\sqrt{34}.
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $f(x,y,z):$

$$f(r(u,v))=(u+2v)-(u-2v)=4v.$$

Therefore, our surface integral can be written as

$$\begin{aligned}\iint_S(x-y)\,\text{d}S&=\iint_D f(r(u,v))‖r_u′\times r_v′‖\,\text{d}A\\&=\sqrt{34}\iint_D 4v\,\text{d}A\\&=\sqrt{34}\int_0^{1}4v\,\text{d}v\cdot\int_0^{3}1\,\text{d}u\\&=\sqrt{34}[2v^{2}]_0^{1}[u]_0^{3}\\&=\sqrt{34}(2-0)(3-0)\\&=6\sqrt{34}.\end{aligned}$$

knowledge_point.title: Evaluating Surface Integrals Over Parametric Surfaces

question.:question/problem:
Evaluate the surface integral

$$\iint_S(x-y)\,\text{d}S,$$

where $r(u,v)=⟨3u+v,\,3u-v,\,v⟩$ for $0\le u\le 3$ and $0\le v\le 3.$

*Hint: $‖r_u′\times r_v′‖=3\sqrt{6}.$*

{{field-1}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the surface integral of a scalar function $f$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A.
$$

Notice that we are told that the norm of the fundamental vector product is

$$
‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖=3\sqrt{6}.
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $f(x,y,z):$

$$f(r(u,v))=(3u+v)-(3u-v)=2v.$$

Therefore, our surface integral can be written as

$$\begin{aligned}\iint_S(x-y)\,\text{d}S&=\iint_D f(r(u,v))‖r_u′\times r_v′‖\,\text{d}A\\&=3\sqrt{6}\iint_D 2v\,\text{d}A\\&=3\sqrt{6}\int_0^{3}2v\,\text{d}v\cdot\int_0^{3}1\,\text{d}u\\&=3\sqrt{6}[v^{2}]_0^{3}[u]_0^{3}\\&=3\sqrt{6}(9-0)(3-0)\\&=81\sqrt{6}.\end{aligned}$$

question.:question/problem:
Evaluate the surface integral

$$\iint_S(x-y)\,\text{d}S,$$

where $r(u,v)=⟨u+v,\,u-v,\,3v⟩$ for $0\le u\le 2$ and $0\le v\le 1.$

*Hint: $‖r_u′\times r_v′‖=\sqrt{22}.$*

{{field-1}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the surface integral of a scalar function $f$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A.
$$

Notice that we are told that the norm of the fundamental vector product is

$$
‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖=\sqrt{22}.
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $f(x,y,z):$

$$f(r(u,v))=(u+v)-(u-v)=2v.$$

Therefore, our surface integral can be written as

$$\begin{aligned}\iint_S(x-y)\,\text{d}S&=\iint_D f(r(u,v))‖r_u′\times r_v′‖\,\text{d}A\\&=\sqrt{22}\iint_D 2v\,\text{d}A\\&=\sqrt{22}\int_0^{1}2v\,\text{d}v\cdot\int_0^{2}1\,\text{d}u\\&=\sqrt{22}[v^{2}]_0^{1}[u]_0^{2}\\&=\sqrt{22}(1-0)(2-0)\\&=2\sqrt{22}.\end{aligned}$$
